- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:~2540-2544 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: mark_candidate_records_for_prune returns a fresh prune_marked_at timestamp even when no records were newly marked.
  WHY: The no-op output still looks like a write occurred; deepseek labeled it NIT while minimax and grok labeled it MAJOR.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:~2210-2248 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: _embedding_search_records sends all valid record texts in one unbounded embedding batch without chunking or a ceiling tied to max_records.
  WHY: Large stores can exceed provider batch/token limits and force the embedding search to fail or fall back to keyword mode after paying the full batching cost.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:~2220, ~2582 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: When every valid record has empty searchable text, search_memory_records still reports method="embedding" and a non-zero searched_record_count even though no embedding API call was made.
  WHY: The payload makes an empty-text no-op look like a successful embedding search instead of signaling that nothing was sent to the API.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:~2544, ~2790 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: mark_candidate_records_for_prune and compact_memory can race on the same candidate record without an explicit distributed lock or idempotency key.
  WHY: Concurrent prune and compact runs can unlink or read the same record out of order.
- scripts/ai_memory.py:~160-200, ~310-340 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The cmd_review and cmd_search MemoryGitError path reports ok: true with a warning and exit code 0, and the branch-missing case is treated as enabled: false silently.
  WHY: Automation cannot distinguish an unavailable ai-memory branch from success.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:~2363-2444 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: search_memory_records does a full canonical and candidate walk plus an embedding batch on every search call.
  WHY: Search cost grows linearly with store size and can exceed CLI timeouts and API quotas.
- scripts/label_helpers.sh:~65-111 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The ai:security-audit and ai:security entries were removed from the helper catalog.
  WHY: Security-audit workflow, label-repair, and tests expect those labels; removing them breaks the label contract.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: ~2542, return dict from mark_candidate_records_for_prune
  Problem: The function always computes resolved_prune_marked_at (from caller or utc_now_iso()) and includes it in the return dict regardless of whether any records were actually marked. When marked is empty because all requested IDs were already-marked or not-found, prune_marked_at still carries a fresh UTC timestamp.
  Why it fails at runtime: The CLI (cmd_prune in scripts/ai_memory.py) propagates this timestamp to its JSON output unchanged. An operator who requested pruning of already-pruned records sees a fresh timestamp under prune_marked_at alongside marked: [] — the timestamp is false because no disk write occurred. This violates the output contract's idempotency signal.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: ~2225-2238, _embedding_search_records
  Problem: The batched embeddings path collects ALL valid records into a single API call before sorting by similarity and truncating to max_records. There is no cap on the batch size. OpenRouter and OpenAI embeddings endpoints have documented limits on input token count (typically ~8192 tokens) and array size (typically ~2048 inputs). A memory store with hundreds or thousands of records can exceed these limits.
  Why it fails at runtime: When the batch exceeds the API limit, _create_memory_search_embeddings raises RuntimeError, caught by search_memory_records at line 2584. The search silently degrades to keyword mode with fallback_reason set. The operator gets keyword results when embedding was requested, and the degradation is only visible by inspecting the fallback_reason field. Large stores pay a high latency/cost penalty for the batch call even when only 10 results are needed.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: ~2220 (record_texts empty check), ~2582 (method = "embedding")
  Problem: When _embedding_search_records returns ([], model) because every valid record in the store has empty summary and details text, search_memory_records still reports method: "embedding" with searched_record_count equaling the total validated record count. The operator cannot distinguish "API call succeeded, no semantic matches" from "no records had searchable text, API was never called."
  Why it fails at runtime: search_memory_records enters the embedding branch at line 2575 because api_key is set and records is non-empty. _embedding_search_records sees zero record_texts and returns early at line 2220 with ([], model). The method stays "embedding" and searched_record_count is non-zero, so the output payload looks like a successful-but-empty embedding search when in fact no embedding API call was made. The result is semantically correct (no matches), but the diagnostic signal is misleading.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: ~2225-2238, _embedding_search_records
  Problem: Same unbounded batch issue as CORRECTNESS finding #2. All valid records are embedded in a single API call regardless of max_records. For stores with thousands of candidate and canonical records, the embeddings API call processes far more text than needed, consuming API tokens, bandwidth, and time.
  Why it fails at runtime: An operator running search --max 10 on a store with 5000 records pays for 5000 embeddings when only 10 results are returned. The embeddings API charges per input token regardless of how many results are kept. This is wasteful but not a crash — the fallback to keyword mode on API failure provides a safety net.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- Requirement: "Add a pyproject.toml / tests/test_ai_memory_cli.py covering each new subcommand on a fixture branch" (plan acceptance criteria); "All four subcommands work against a fixture ai-memory branch in tests/test_ai_memory_cli.py" (plan lines 820-823).
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml — the explicit python3 tests/<file>.py allowlist that gates which tests run in CI.
  Evidence of absence: tests/test_ai_memory_cli.py exists and contains 7 tests covering review, prune, compact, search (keyword and embedding), and export. However, the repo's CI workflows use explicit per-file invocations (python3 tests/<file>.py) rather than pytest discovery. A grep for test_ai_memory_cli across .github/workflows/ returns zero matches. The pyproject.toml pytest configuration does not help because CI never invokes pytest. Without adding this file to the allowlist, the new test suite never executes in CI and the acceptance criterion cannot be verified automatically.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- Requirement: "Keep this phase tool-only: no workflow behavior changes and no new persistent maintenance channel." (Linked Issue #3517)
  Expected change site: .ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt
  Evidence of absence: The original PR diff (visible in the full PR patch but not in the last run diff) adds six entries to .ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt that are not Phase G ai-memory CLI deliverables: .github/workflows/security-audit.yml, prompts/contracts/mode-security-audit.yml, prompts/mode-security-audit.txt, scripts/security_audit.sh, scripts/security_audit_fp_exclusions.json, and tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py. These are security-audit project files from a different phase. Phase G is explicitly scoped to four CLI subcommands, a test harness, and agents.md documentation. The security-audit files constitute scope creep that introduces workflow and script artifacts the linked issue forbids. The last run diff did not touch the manifest, so these entries persist on HEAD.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: lines 2540-2543 in `mark_candidate_records_for_prune` function
  Problem: The function always returns `"prune_marked_at": resolved_prune_marked_at` even when no records were newly marked (all were `already_marked` or `not_found`). The returned timestamp is misleading because it suggests a write occurred when actually zero records were touched.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators using the CLI see a timestamp in the JSON output indicating a commit happened, but `did_commit: false` and empty `marked` array show nothing was actually written. This creates confusion about whether the operation succeeded.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
